sections.h2: Where Ellis County deed records are held
sections.html:
The County Clerk records real property instruments. The office is on the second floor of 109 S. Jackson St. in Waxahachie, and mail goes to P.O. Box 250, Waxahachie 75168. The property recording line is 972-825-5070, the fax is 972-825-5075, and the counter serves the public on weekdays between eight in the morning and four-thirty in the afternoon.

Anything that touches title lands in this office: every kind of deed, plus leases, sale contracts and powers of attorney tied to local land.

The same office files birth, death, marriage and military discharge records, handles probate and guardianship filings and serves as clerk of the Commissioners Court. Passports, divorces and felony matters belong to the District Clerk instead.

Clerks may not give legal advice or prepare an instrument for you (Government Code Sec. 81.101). Arrive with a finished document that shows a return address, or let a title company file it.

The Recording Division page offers eRecording through approved vendors, and the county links a public records search. Filing electronically saves a drive to Waxahachie.

Since January 1, 2024 the first page of a recorded document is $25.00, and each added page, part of a page or rider is $4.00. Senate Bill 1612 repealed the separate $1.00 document filing fee, which is why the first-page charge dropped to that level.

sections.h2: Payments and copies at the counter
sections.html:
Make checks payable to the Ellis County Clerk. Cards and debit are accepted with a processing charge of 2.4 percent or $1, whichever is larger. A returned check costs $25.00, a check older than 90 days is refused, and refunds wait for the check to clear.

  • Noncertified paper copy or paper-to-electronic conversion: $1.00 per page or part of a page.
  • Electronic copy of an electronic document: $1.00 up to 10 pages, then $0.10 for each added page.
  • Certification: $5.00. Full-size plat copy: $10.00.

Copy rates fall under Local Government Code Sec. 118.0145, and the certification fee under Sec. 118.014.

Ellis County had 240,867 people in mid-2025 across 935.75 land square miles, up 25.2 percent since 2020. The 2020 and 2010 counts were 192,455 and 149,610. The county has 15 cities, 7 towns and unincorporated communities including Avalon, Forreston and Telico, and many owners work elsewhere in the Dallas area and live here for space. Median household income is $99,595 for 2020 to 2024.

For a seller, the useful point is that the address may sit in any of those cities or in the country, so the school district and taxing units differ from parcel to parcel. Confirm yours on the appraisal district's parcel page.

sections.h2: Older deeds and the Waxahachie courthouse
sections.html:
Texas carved the county out of Navarro County on December 20, 1849, and the seat was named Waxahachie. Records here run back a long way, and the present courthouse, accepted in 1897, is the fourth on the site. Earlier buildings included an 1850 log cabin, a frame building in 1854 and a limestone courthouse around 1870.

If a legal description looks unusual, ask your title company to trace older deeds back as far as needed.

sections.h2: Who appraises property and where to pay
sections.html:
The Ellis Appraisal District sets value. The Ellis County Tax Office at 302 N. Monroe St., Waxahachie, phone 972-825-5150, can give contact details for each taxing unit. The appraisal district maintains parcel data and ownership downloads.

The appraisal district offers an online portal for property alerts, plus pages for filing a protest and booking an informal appointment. A tax transparency site shows proposed rates from each unit in late summer. Taxing units adopt the rates, not the appraisal district. Value and rate together make the bill.

The state levies no property tax of its own. Value is measured every January 1, notices reach homesteads first in spring, protests close in mid-May and bills arrive in the fall.

sections.h2: What a title search turns up
sections.html:
• Vesting deed. The grantee on the last recorded deed should be the seller.
  • Lien releases. A paid mortgage can linger in the index until a release is filed.
  • Tax liens. Federal and state liens are recorded by the clerk under the fees above.
  • Heirs. A property passed by death may need an executor's deed, a death-transfer deed, a muniment order or an affidavit of heirship, depending on how the estate was handled.

Recording needs a signature plus a notary-style acknowledgment or two witnesses. After a death the clerk cannot amend the earlier deed to list heirs. A new instrument must carry them.

Ellis County is served by Avalon, Ennis, Ferris, Italy, Maypearl, Midlothian, Milford, Palmer, Red Oak and Waxahachie school districts. The district a house sits in affects the school tax portion of the bill.

sections.h2: Preparing to record an Ellis County sale
sections.html:
A little prep keeps the recording day short. Confirm the seller's name matches the last recorded deed, print the grantee's mailing address, and make sure the notary has completed the acknowledgment before you leave the table. Put a return address on the document so the clerk can send it back.

Bring a check made out to the Ellis County Clerk, and add the extra $4.00 for each page after the first. If the deed runs onto a second page with only a signature block, you still pay for it. For a house with a mortgage, the lender's payoff and the release of lien usually come through the title company, so ask who files each one and when.

A cash sale skips the lender paperwork, which leaves fewer instruments to record. The deed, any prior lien release and the tax payoff are usually the whole list.

Buyers closing in spring or summer should ask the appraisal district about claiming a homestead right away, because an exemption can start mid-year when the seller never held one. School districts exempt $140,000 of a residence's value, and seniors and disabled owners get another $60,000 plus a school tax ceiling.

Appraised value of a homestead may rise only 10 percent a year once the exemption has been in place a full year. Heirs missing from the recorded deed must give the district an affidavit, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

faqs.q: Which office files a deed for an Ellis County house?
faqs.a: Record it with the County Clerk at 109 S. Jackson St., 2nd Floor, Waxahachie, or send it through an approved eRecording vendor. The property recording line is 972-825-5070.

faqs.q: What will recording a deed cost in Ellis County?
faqs.a: Page one is $25.00, and each later page, partial page or rider adds $4.00. Every name past five adds a quarter.

faqs.q: Can the Ellis County Clerk prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff may not advise on law or draft an instrument, so hire a lawyer or a title firm to write it.

faqs.q: What are the Ellis County Clerk's hours?
faqs.a: Monday to Friday, eight to four-thirty. County offices also close on observed holidays, so call 972-825-5070 before a trip.

faqs.q: Which Ellis County office mails a tax statement?
faqs.a: Statements come from the county tax office on behalf of the taxing units, and the appraisal district does not bill. The Ellis County Tax Office is at 302 N. Monroe St., Waxahachie, phone 972-825-5150.
